title: Genesis
author: Moses is traditionally understood as the author of Genesis as part of the Pentateuch.
date: Traditionally connected with the time of Moses, commonly placed in the second millennium B.C.
audience: The covenant people of Israel, teaching them the beginning of creation, humanity, sin, judgment, promise, and God's covenant purposes.
historicalSetting: Genesis begins with creation and traces the history of humanity from Adam to Noah, then narrows to the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. It prepares Israel to understand their covenant identity and God's redemptive promises.
themes: God as Creator of all things
Human sin and the need for redemption
God's providence over suffering and history
keyVerse: Genesis 12:3 — "All of the families of the earth will be blessed in you."
christFocus: Genesis points to Christ from the first promise of the seed of the woman who would bruise the serpent's head, through the covenant promise that all nations would be blessed through Abraham's seed. It shows the need for redemption and begins the unfolding story that finds its fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
outline: Creation and the beginning of humanity — Genesis 1-2
The fall, judgment, and first promise of redemption — Genesis 3-5
Noah, the flood, and God's covenant mercy — Genesis 6-11
Abraham and the covenant promise — Genesis 12-25
Joseph and God's providence in Egypt — Genesis 37-50
